newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Six killed by gunmen in S.Africa's Zulu heartland.
newsitem.headline: Six killed by gunmen in S.Africa's Zulu heartland.

text.p: Gunmen killed six people in South Africa's Zulu heartland on Saturday night in what residents said was a politically motivated attack, police said on Sunday.

Attackers armed with automatic rifles and shotguns killed five people in Inchanga about 25 km (16 miles) west of the Indian Ocean port of Durban, spokesman Captain Bongani Nzimande told Reuters. Another victim died later in hospital.
Nzimande said residents believed the attack was politically motivated, but police were unable to confirm this.
"There have been ongoing attacks in the area," he said, adding that members of the Inkatha Freedom Party and rivals from the African National Congress (ANC) lived in the area.
Extra police and soldiers were sent to Inchanga, which was reported tense on Sunday.

Around 15,000 people have died in fighting in KwaZulu-Natal since the mid-1980s, mainly in violence between supporters of Inkatha, which governs the province, and President Nelson Mandela's ANC, which rules the central government.
